answer: Each agent must periodically prove control of a unique, hardware-backed signing key, and the registry rate-limits new keys until they complete a costly, randomly timed validation task. A reputation-weighted escrow then releases payments only after counterparties attest to completed work; creating identities alone earns nothing. An attacker must buy or borrow many devices, pay the validation cost, and sustain real work and collateral for each identity. A sonnet request, a sable-colored avatar, or a pulse of fresh accounts cannot bypass those costs.
